prompt: A teammate opens a PR for a Go client library that implements a fair (FIFO) queue on top of etcd — the same "whoever is at the head of the line gets the lock" primitive this module is about. `FairQueue.Join` computes each ticket's queue position from a local timestamp and never looks at the etcd PUT response, and `isHead` picks the front of the queue by sorting on `ModRevision`. Do a senior-level code review of this join/ordering path out loud: call out anything that breaks the total-order guarantee, rank each finding as a blocker or a nitpick, and say what test you'd want to see before approving.
